questions.q: What problem does an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) primarily address, in Team Topologies' framing?
options: It guarantees zero production incidents across every service
It replaces stream-aligned teams entirely with a centralized operations team
It reduces the cognitive load on stream-aligned teams by absorbing complexity they'd otherwise have to understand and operate themselves
It eliminates the need for any infrastructure knowledge anywhere in the organization
questions.explain: Cognitive load is the finite mental capacity a team has for understanding and operating systems. A platform absorbs complexity that would otherwise sit on every stream-aligned team's plate so that capacity is freed for the actual business problem.

questions.q: Without a shared platform, what commonly happens across teams building and deploying services independently, per this lesson?
options: Each team re-solves the same Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI problems, producing inconsistent, expensive-to-maintain 'snowflake' systems
Teams converge naturally on identical tooling without any coordination
Onboarding time shrinks because every team's setup is unique
Security posture automatically improves because each team fully controls its own stack
questions.explain: Ten teams each independently deriving their own production-readiness decisions doesn't produce ten slightly different setups — it produces ten snowflake systems, each expensive to secure, patch, and support.

questions.q: How does CNCF describe the output of the platform engineering discipline — the Internal Developer Platform itself?
options: A mandatory set of rules enforced purely through audits
A one-time migration project with a fixed end date
A ticketing system that routes every infrastructure request to a human on the ops team
A consolidated layer that packages provisioning, deployment tooling, and operational capabilities behind a self-service interface
questions.explain: CNCF's definition centers on self-service: an IDP consolidates provisioning and operational tooling so teams consume it directly, rather than assembling raw cloud primitives themselves or waiting on a ticket queue.

questions.q: Which best characterizes the difference between platform engineering and classic reactive ops/sysadmin work, as this lesson frames it?
options: There is no meaningful difference; it is a rebrand with no new practices
Platform engineering outsources all infrastructure decisions to individual developers
Platform engineering only applies to organizations with fewer than ten engineers
Platform engineering treats what it builds as a product with users and a roadmap, not just infrastructure kept running on a ticket-by-ticket basis
questions.explain: Traditional ops work is reactive — keep systems running, respond to tickets. Platform engineering is a product-engineering discipline aimed inward, measured by adoption and developer outcomes, not just uptime.

questions.q: Why is cognitive load specifically the right unit of measurement, rather than just 'how much infrastructure exists'?
options: Because infrastructure amount is irrelevant as long as documentation exists somewhere
Because the issue isn't that infrastructure exists, it's whose mental capacity is spent understanding and operating it — a platform team's, once, or every stream-aligned team's, repeatedly
Because cognitive load only affects junior engineers, not senior ones
Because Terraform and Kubernetes have no learning curve once installed
questions.explain: Cognitive load asks whose capacity a given piece of complexity currently sits on, and whether it's cheaper in aggregate for one platform team to carry it than for every stream-aligned team to carry its own copy.
